text:
lin: quick follow-up to the control-plane split RFC. we need to choose how we expose the control plane into customer VPCs: long-lived private endpoints (persistent privatelink/ENI) vs ephemeral, tokenized endpoints that are created on-demand and rotated. want to capture operational, security, and customer UX tradeoffs.

dez: short summary plz?

lin: persistent endpoints = customers get a stable IP/ENI or privatelink endpoint in their account. easy for firewall allowlists and vendor approvals. downside: ENI/NAT quotas, drift, lifecycle ops (certificate rotation, stale endpoints) and higher baseline infra cost. ephemeral endpoints = we provision short-lived interface endpoints (or handshake via mTLS tokens) when control-plane traffic originates; cleaner quotas, easier cleanup, but customers must accept dynamic IPs or DNS allowlist and more complex handoff flows.

parker: ops perspective: persistent endpoints mean we need reconciliation loops to detect drift and auto-heal, plus an onboarding job that requests ENI attachments per customer. scaled to 10k tenants these will hit quotas fast. ephemeral approach uses fewer persistent AWS objects but increases API chatter and provisioning latency.

sana: security/compliance: persistent endpoints simplify audits since endpoint artifact exists in customer account. ephemeral endpoints require robust attestation and short cert TTLs + revocation lists to make auditors comfortable. also leakage detection is harder for ephemeral unless we log every handshake.

rita: customer UX: many customers ask for a stable private IP to raise a ticket with a partner. if we go ephemeral by default, we need a documented "sticky" upgrade path for customers that require stability. sales will want a clear SLA and provisioning timeline for sticky mode.

devx: DNS is a big lever here. with split-horizon DNS and low TTLs we can provide a stable DNS name while rotating the underlying endpoint addresses. that lets partners allowlist names via DNS-based allowlist solutions. downside: some firewall appliances don't support DNS-based allowlists.

ops-bot: quota_cost_snapshot: tenants=1200; persistent_endpoints_est_monthly="~$48k (ENI+privatelink)+quota ops"; ephemeral_est_monthly="~$9.6k (provisioning API + short-lived endpoints)"; expected_provision_latency_s="~1.2s (cold) / 60ms (warm pool)".

parker: latency note: ephemeral cold-provision path adds ~1s to control-plane calls during initial handshake. we can mitigate with a warm pool per-region that keeps N idle endpoints ready to attach. warm pool costs are lower than ENI per-tenant baseline.

sana: rotation + revocation plan for ephemeral: issue client certs with 10m TTL, rotate control-plane leaf certs every 6h, maintain a signed revocation list in the control plane pushed to customers' sidecar agents. need clear forensic logs for auditor queries.

lin: proposal: default = ephemeral tokenized endpoints with split-horizon DNS and warm pool optimization. provide a "stable-endpoint" enterprise addon (persistent privatelink/ENI or customer-managed privatelink) for customers who need a fixed IP. keep default provisioning fast and low-cost.

rita: agree in principle. product asks: SLA for stable-endpoint provisioning? can we commit <48h?

parker: provisioning pipeline estimate: automated provisioning + cross-account privatelink handshake + cert sync = typically <24h if quotas OK; we should default to <48h SLA. need a manual approval path for quota exceptions.

devx: on DNS flow, we should document fallback when customer DNS doesn't support split-horizon: use ephemeral with header-based tenant tags + partner coordination. also call out SNI implications for TCP passthrough.

sana: monitoring checklist for ephemeral: endpoint_provision_latency, warm_pool_usage, cert_reissue_rate, handshake_failure_rate, endpoint_leak_alerts (detect interfaces that stay active past expected TTL).

lin: lifecycle decisions: when we deprovision a tenant we must revoke all active tokens, tear down warm pools, and mark endpoints deprecated for 24h before final delete to allow in-flight connections to drain. add a hard-delete path for emergency offboards.

rita: legal/compliance will require an audit log export for stable-endpoint customers showing cert issuance history and revocations for 2 years. add to product requirements.

ops-bot: action_created: rfc_addendum_ephemeral_default, owner=lin, due_ts=1736081955

parker: next engineering spikes: 1) warm-pool autoscaler and attach/detach latency tests (parker+devx), 2) attestation token design + revocation list (sana+lin), 3) onboarding flow for stable-endpoint SLA <48h (rita+parker).

lin: +1 to those spikes. i'll draft the RFC addendum accordingly and include a migration playbook for customers on persistent endpoints to move to ephemeral sticky-mode.

devx: +1. please also add a short customer-facing doc snippet explaining DNS options and what to expect during provisioning.

parker: +1
